titulo: Your space heater doesn't belong on a power strip.
receta: regla con numero (3 feet) + pregunta de si/no; pilar home safety, invierno
destinatario: se lo manda alguien que vive con un calefactor a su companero de cuarto que lo enchufa a la regleta de la compu
regla_guardable: Space heater: wall outlet only, three feet from anything that burns, off when you sleep.

interaccion.guardar: Space heater: wall outlet only, never a power strip or extension cord; 3 feet from anything that can burn; never on while you sleep or leave.
interaccion.comentar: Do you run a space heater at home? Yes or no?

fuentes: U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission, OnSafety blog 'Your space heater needs space' (onsafety.cpsc.gov/blog/2017/01/13/your-space-heater-needs-space/): 'Do not use extension cords or power strips with space heaters, to reduce the risk of fires'; keep curtains, sofas, beds, clothes and papers at least three feet away; 'Never leave the heater on while unattended, or while sleeping.'

U.S. Fire Administration (FEMA), Space Heater Safety Tips pictograph (usfa.fema.gov/gallery/pictographs/pictograph41.html): 'Plug space heaters directly into wall outlets and never into an extension cord or power strip.'

frases.texto: That space heater is plugged into a power strip.
frases.estilo: Dry and punchy, with a half smile.

frases.texto: The Consumer Product Safety Commission says: do not use extension cords or power strips with space heaters.
The U.S. Fire Administration says plug it directly into a wall outlet.
Keep it at least three feet from curtains, beds, sofas, clothes and papers.
Heads up: never leave it on while it's unattended, or while you're sleeping.
Save this: wall outlet only, three feet of space, and off when you sleep.
